title: Open a cold domain with an ungated build
statement: When learners arrive with no usable background in a unit's domain, make its first lesson an ungated knowledge build, say so, and start comprehension gates in the next lesson.
example: Three breadth units in one course, on space, ancient Rome and the United States, each opened with a gate-free build.
detail: Archived prompts for a Grade 3 reading course mark three breadth units as pre-teach-heavy, because a Grade 3 reader arrives with no usable astronomy, ancient-history or U.S. geography and civics base (`incept-package-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v2/authoring/prompts`, units 7, 8 and 9). In each, the first lesson is a gate-free knowledge build that lays the base before any comprehension gate, and gates start in the second lesson; the space unit's prompt says that without the build the second lesson's gate would sit on nothing, and tells the writer to state plainly in the lesson that the build is gate-free and that gates begin next lesson. The course's authoring preamble and a later Grade 6 contract keep the rule for a cold-domain opener: the on-ramp expands into a gate-free knowledge build, and the lesson says so.
against: The prompts are archived and record no results for these lessons.
